note: HUMAN_PROMPTS.md row 17, run as a task: the prompt adds an explicit go-ahead so the agent implements instead of only explaining. Template has no Code Mode yet, so this covers setup + an async approval interceptor on the acme submit_payment tool.

input.prompt: Can I make Code Mode ask me before it submits a payment? If so, please set it up.
input.reply: Show me a confirmation in the app with the payment details before any submit_payment call goes through, and block it if I decline. Use your recommended defaults for everything else.

rubric: Enables Code Mode exactly once for this assistant, in the AI Web configuration io.Assist uses (aiWebConfig in app/src/App.tsx), not in the acme MCP server
Uses the browser entry point and points the WASM location at a URL the app serves, delivered from the installed @interopio/code-mode package through a repeatable step or an exact-version URL
Adds an asynchronous interceptors.onToolCall on that Code Mode configuration that awaits the user's decision before submit_payment runs
Matches submit_payment by the tool identifier the host actually passes to the interceptor (verified in docs or installed types), not a guessed name
Shows the payment details from the call input (client, amount, currency, beneficiary) in the approval prompt
Fails closed: a declined, dismissed or failed approval denies the call, and approval is never assumed or auto-granted
Lets every other tool call through unchanged and does not add a toolFilter or rewrite the payment input
Leaves submit_payment's server-side validation in mcp-server intact
Explains in the final message that the interceptor only gates calls made through Code Mode, so the server must still authorize and validate payments
[report-only] Uses the io.Connect modals dialogs that the app already enables instead of window.confirm
[report-only] Chooses the @interopio/code-mode version from the npm registry and the installed host's range, not from a docs example
